explanation: The Edict is what Ferdinand did with the Danish war won, and the article says so in its first four words: "Made overconfident by success, in March 1629, Ferdinand passed an Edict of Restitution." Wolgast is the last of the defeats that success is made of — "Von Arnim abandoned the siege on 4 August, but three weeks later Christian suffered another defeat at Wolgast. He began negotiations with Wallenstein" — and the negotiations became the Treaty of Lübeck in June 1629, three months before the Edict. Precondition-of: the confidence, not the battle, is what the article makes the cause.
